A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ControlAudio work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, allowing additions to be distinguished reliably from relocated content.

before.justification: v2 reports original audio-generation benchmarks, prompt and vocabulary ablations, sampling analyses, and subjective evaluation outcomes in Section 5 and Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds category-wise AudioCondition results and transition-timestep sensitivity results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The data-construction pipeline, unified text/timing/phoneme representation, three-stage DiT training and two-phase guided sampling remain unchanged. The new pseudocode and main-text LLM-planning explanation document procedures already described in v2.

E1.justification: Appendix A retains the same training corpora and simulated scenarios. Evaluation still covers AudioCondition, AC-Filtered, AudioCaps, LibriTTS-R and LibriSpeech. The new category breakdown and timestep sweep introduce no additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–5 is unchanged. New Table 8 disaggregates the existing AudioCondition comparison with FreeAudio. Newly cited methods such as PicoAudio2, DegDiT and UmbraTTS are discussed as related work but are not added to the reported evaluations.

E3.justification: Tables 9–10 add a transition-timestep evaluation grid: 100, 95, 90, 85 and 80, plus a finer sweep from 90 to 85. The default remains t1 = 88 with 100 sampling steps. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and subjective-evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds category-wise temporal-performance analysis and coarse/fine sensitivity analysis of the sampling transition timestep. These examine variation across sound categories and the robustness of the selected transition point, supplementing the retained prompt, vocabulary and guidance-scale studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new result tables follow the same reporting practice; the 20-evaluator MOS design is retained.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged. New Table 8 reports category scores, including speech Eb of 64.23 for ControlAudio versus 39 for FreeAudio. Table 9 newly reports FAD/WER of 5.82/5.98 at t1 = 100 and 3.35/7.67 at t1 = 80; these are sensitivity results under different sampling settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, including the diffusion objective, sampling factorization and learning-rate formula, are retained. The new algorithms summarize existing procedures without introducing a theorem, proof or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims. The introduction still presents unified timing-controlled, intelligible audio generation through progressive data construction, training and sampling.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 replaces the claimed contrast with complex TTS duration prediction with an explanation acknowledging established duration conditioning. v3 adds interpretations of category performance and timestep sensitivity. However, Section 5.3 says larger t1 harms intelligibility, contradicting Tables 9–10 and Appendix E.2. The limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly discloses training budgets of 1M, 0.5M and 0.5M steps, eight NVIDIA A800 GPUs and total batch size 128. Appendix D adds training and inference pseudocode, and Section 5.2 clarifies use of the public AudioComposer-Small variant. These are documentation additions, without evidence of revised existing training settings.

R1.justification: Sections 2 and 4.3 update related work with recent controllable-audio, TTS and progressive-generation studies, including PicoAudio2, DegDiT, UmbraTTS and F5-TTS. The discussion acknowledges related audio applications of progressive modeling and shared duration-conditioning ideas while retaining the central positioning around unified timing and speech control.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted rewrites to related work, the duration rationale and results discussion, and adds main-text planning and implementation summaries plus acknowledgments. New Appendices D and E precede the retained planning and transcription appendices, now F and G. Most of the narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 8–10 and two algorithm displays. The existing LLM-planning diagram moves from the appendix to Section 4.3 and is resized, becoming Figure 3; the guidance plot becomes Figure 4. Existing tables are rearranged, and the planning examples remain as Table 11. The figures themselves retain their content.

improvement.justification: The newly disclosed training budgets and compute, procedural pseudocode, and category/timestep analyses improve reproducibility and empirical transparency. Section 4.3 also gives a more qualified account of the relationship to TTS duration conditioning. These provide a limited net improvement, although the new contradiction between Section 5.3 and Appendix E.2 weakens clarity about the sampling trade-off.
